summary: @lyxa.ai/core bootstrapCore hardcodes author-owned CloudAMQP broker as the event bus
details: The exported bootstrapCore() entry point in dist/index.js unconditionally connects amqplib to a hardcoded amqps:// URL on dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com with baked-in username and password, then wires the caller's @SubscribeToEvent handlers to that broker. Any application invoking the advertised bootstrap API publishes its event payloads to, and consumes messages from, an author-controlled RabbitMQ instance the caller neither chose nor configured, with no code path to override the broker URL. Because the broker credentials are shipped in the tarball, anyone who reads the package can also publish messages that installer subscription handlers will process as trusted events. The package documents itself as a generic 'core' framework module, so the relay to a specific third-party broker is not the disclosed purpose of the API.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
